message.content:
A reflection matrix over a line making angle \(\theta\) with the \(x\)-axis has the form
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos 2\theta & \sin 2\theta\\
\sin 2\theta & -\cos 2\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Comparing with
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
-\frac{7}{25} & \frac{24}{25}\\
\frac{24}{25} & \frac{7}{25}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
we get
\[
\cos 2\theta = -\frac{7}{25}, \qquad \sin 2\theta = \frac{24}{25}.
\]

Let \(t=\tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}\). Then
\[
\cos 2\theta = \frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}.
\]
So
\[
\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}=-\frac{7}{25}.
\]
Solving:
\[
25(1-t^2)=-7(1+t^2)
\]
\[
25-25t^2=-7-7t^2
\]
\[
32=18t^2
\]
\[
t^2=\frac{16}{9}.
\]
Thus \(t=\pm \frac{4}{3}\). Since
\[
\sin 2\theta = \frac{2t}{1+t^2}=\frac{24}{25}>0,
\]
we need \(t>0\). Therefore,
\[
\frac{y}{x}=\frac{4}{3}.
\]

The answer is \(\frac{4}{3}\).
